feedback: No earlier race exists, so this feedback has no outcome evidence. What I had to decide in the controller: the five-sensor row spans 48 mm against a 25 mm tape, so the centre sensors cover the line at all times, but the outer pair only reads the tape when the line is near the edge. The steering signal therefore stays small and proportional when the robot is centred. The 40 mm look-ahead means the line is sensed before the wheels reach it, which should reduce lag, but it also means the controller acts on a path the wheels have not yet covered. Hold the current geometry for iteration 1 so the first race gives a clean baseline. Then decide as follows. If the race shows saturated or near-saturated outer readings with high line-loss counts on tight bends, try a narrower span (for example x pitch 0.008 m, giving ±0.016 m) so the line stays within the sensor range at the cost of earlier saturation. If steering_oscillation is high at speed but line loss is low, try a longer look-ahead (y near 0.06) to give the controller more time to respond. If rms_error is low and both are fine, keep the geometry and let tuning carry the score.
requested_changes: Hold the current geometry for iteration 1 to get a clean baseline; change nothing until race data shows which limit binds.
If line_loss_events are high on tight bends, try sensor x pitch 0.008 m (x = -0.016 to +0.016) to keep the line within the sensor range.
